tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of arXiv agent-RL papers, not one developing story. Since Oct 20 it has collected work on rollout cost, search and RAG agents, and a split over fine-grained credit assignment.
whats_new: Nov 4: an arXiv study finds multi-turn RL gains for LLM agents depend heavily on sampling breadth K and interaction depth, and Nov 3 adds guidance-stabilization and web-agent RL papers.
why_it_matters: Agent RL results are sensitive to rollout budget, numerical setup and reward granularity, so a reported gain may not transfer to your harness. All are paper-reported, not production evidence.

status.detail: A loose set of agentic-RL papers; the newest tests what multi-turn RL actually improves.

beats.headline: Rollout budgets and numerical stability set the cost of agent RL
beats.summary: Budget allocation, environment-aware scheduling, BF16 rounding alignment, and a managed SageMaker recipe.

beats.headline: Search, data and RAG agents get RL recipes with self-assessment and calibration
Credit assignment: finer signals help in some settings and hurt in others
beats.summary: Twin-world and token-level credit compete with a video-editing study showing finer credit can fail.

beats.headline: Error-targeted training, co-evolved harnesses and skill routing for tool agents
Neighboring RL work: simulation, robustness, explainability, compression, flow models
Multi-turn RL gains depend on sampling breadth and interaction depth

open_questions: Do the multi-turn RL findings hold when sampling breadth and interaction depth are fixed to your production limits?
Do the credit-assignment findings from video editing hold on text-only tool-use agents?
Do reward-disagreement rollout budgets cut cost on agents outside the MCP benchmark?
Does co-evolving the harness with the policy beat a fixed harness on independent tasks?
take_for_builders: Before adopting any of these recipes, rerun them at your own sampling breadth and turn limits, and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat all results as unreplicated.
